mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is causally linked to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of observations when FEDFUNDS < 3.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% over a 3-month period signals economic weakness that triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.5pp in 3 months over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS rise >1.0% in 1 month over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.25% in one month signals aggressive monetary tightening that causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% in 1 month over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by rising non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS), is causally linked to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days, as it supports consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when PAYEMS > 134,000 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 over a 3-month period signals a manufacturing slowdown that causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when INDPRO falls < 105.0 in 3 months over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of instances where both GDPC1 and HOUST decline >0.5% in 3 months over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL YoY growth < 1.5%), a stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% in one month) signals a benign economic environment that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days.
regime_hint: low inflation with stable monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY growth < 1.5% and FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% in 1 month over any 2-year rolling window.
